title: fix(release): re-date a pre-written current-series field on its GA's own version run
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DVpDneDXJ9NfqbFvSYEb6Xa)_

Fixes #25356

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

A code PR on one file, `scripts/sync-release-index-currency.mjs` (+322 / -47). It touches no `content/docs/releases/**` file, no workflow and no package.

## What changed

The rewriter refused to touch a `current series:` field that already names the newest GA, date included, on every run. That refusal is right for prerelease cuts: its header records the 17.7.0 field that every `18.0.0-next.N` cut re-dated. It was wrong on one run: the run whose `changeset version` writes the GA's CHANGELOG heading. On that run the run's date is the true one, and a field written by hand ahead of the cut is not. 18.0.0 shipped dated 2026-10-19 that way.

Now:

- **`committedChangelogText(root)`** reads `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` as committed at `HEAD` with `git show` (GIT_* stripped by `gitFreeEnv()`, per `GIT_ENV_ISOLATION_RULE`). It uses no clock and no network. A `HEAD` git cannot read is a refusal, because either default would bring back one of the two defects.
- **`gaVersionRunMajors()`** returns the majors whose newest GA heading is in the working tree and not at `HEAD`. Those are the majors on their GA's own version run.
- **`rewriteStatusField(field, newest, date, { gaVersionRun })`** re-dates a same-version field only when `gaVersionRun` is true. A re-date that changes nothing returns null, so a current index stays unwritten. The refused shapes ("final release:", trailing matter, prose) stay refused on the GA run too.
- **`rewriteIndexText`** now requires `headChangelogText` and refuses without it. A caller that forgot it would otherwise silently get the 18.0.0 behaviour back. `syncIndex` reads it with `committedChangelogText`, so `main()` and the self-test take the same path.
- `main()` labels a re-date in its output: "re-dated: this run's version pass wrote the newest v18 GA heading, so this is its version commit".
- The header has a new section, "The one same-version field it DOES re-date", with the 18.0.0 measurement.

Every other run keeps today's behaviour. A prerelease cut writes only a prerelease heading, which is never a GA. A run with nothing pending writes no heading. A run after the version commit has landed finds the heading at `HEAD`.

## Two refinements of the card's guard, and why

The card words the guard as "the newest GA at HEAD differs from the newest GA after `changeset version`". This PR keeps that idea with two changes:

1. **Per major, not for the whole repository.** On the 18.1.0 run, a v17 field naming 17.7.0 still names 17.x's newest GA. Re-dating it to 18.1.0's day would be the 17.7.0 defect again. Control I pins this on the 18.0.0 shape: v18 is re-dated and v17 is left byte-identical.
2. **"Introduced", not "differs".** A working tree that lost a GA heading `HEAD` carries also "differs", and it is no version commit. The predicate is "this major's newest GA heading is absent at `HEAD`", which is exactly "this run's `changeset version` wrote it". Control I pins the lost-heading case.

## Where it runs, and the governed check

- The script runs only from the root `version` script (`pnpm run version`). release.yml's `version-pr` job runs that twice: in "Render the post-version tree" (line 561) and as changesets/action's `version-script` (line 939). cut-rc.yml runs it on its snapshot (line 473). In all three, `HEAD` is the commit being rendered and the tree is clean before the pass; release.yml already diffs the output against `HEAD` (`git diff --name-only HEAD`). The `version-pr` checkout is shallow (depth 1), which still holds `HEAD`'s tree.
- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --branch claude/project-thread-1r2arf` at `fbd6690`: "governed-surface predicate: 0 of 1 path(s) hit the register (7 surfaces govern objectstack). ✅ NOT governed", size 369 changed lines (≤ 3000). No workflow file changes, so the lane is untouched.

## Proof

**Self-test** (`pnpm check:release-index-currency-sync`, exit 0): "OK self-test: 58 cases pass". Before this change it was 42. The new battery **Control I** (16 cases, floored; roster floor 8 → 9) pins:

- On the GA version run, a pre-written same-version field is re-dated, and the line is byte-for-byte the current entry.
- A **prerelease run** leaves the pre-written field alone. So does a **non-version run** (CHANGELOG at `HEAD` = CHANGELOG in the tree).
- The lost-heading case, the per-major 18.0.0 shape, and the field-level refusals all hold on the GA run.
- `rewriteIndexText` refuses without `headChangelogText`.
- End to end through `syncIndex` on a real throwaway git repository: re-dated on disk on the GA run; left alone after the version commit lands; refused when git cannot read the CHANGELOG at `HEAD`, with the index untouched.

Control H's end-to-end tree is now a real repository too: a prerelease cut on it still writes nothing.

**Rehearsal on the real corpus** (a throwaway repository holding this branch's index, spec CHANGELOG and the four scripts). The v18 field was pre-written by hand to `(current series: 18.1.0, released 2026-10-21)` and committed as `HEAD`. Then `## 18.1.0` was added to the CHANGELOG, as `changeset version` would add it:

| Run | Result |
|:--|:--|
| this branch | `v18: (current series: 18.1.0, released 2026-10-21) → (current series: 18.1.0, released 2026-10-23) — re-dated: …`, exit 0 |
| `origin/main`'s script, same tree | "… nothing rewritten", exit 0, field still `released 2026-10-21` (the 18.0.0 defect) |
| this branch, after committing the version pass, a later date | `{"wrote":false,"rewrites":[],"gaVersionRun":[]}`, field keeps `2026-10-23` |

The live tree: `node scripts/sync-release-index-currency.mjs` prints "every in-scope entry … (v16, v17, v18) already names the newest GA release of its major … nothing rewritten", exit 0, and the tree stays clean.

**The 18.0.0 date this would have stamped.** The Version Packages PR #24524's commit `31abb7184c` was authored 2026-10-20T11:10Z, and npm published 18.0.0 at 2026-10-20T12:51Z (from #25354). So the version run would have stamped 2026-10-20, the true day.

## Gates

At `fbd6690` (this branch merged with `origin/main` `830a63a`), `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 33 commands for the one path. Each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe. On the first pass, six returned PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3: `yaml` and `typescript` not installed in the fresh worktree): `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-closing-keyword-parity` (both modes), `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check:cli-command-ids` and `check:driver-memory-census`. After `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` all six exit 0. `--ran` reconciles: "✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 33 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 33 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED". The script-specific families among them include `check:release-index-currency-sync`, `check-scripts-symbol-anchors` (both modes), `check-self-test-wired` (both modes), `check-self-test-workflow-commands` (both modes), `check:entry-guard`, `check:nul-bytes` and `check:pm-dispatch-gates`.

Run before the push: `check-commit-card-trailers --range origin/main..HEAD` ✓, `check-regen-pending --pre-push` exit 0.

No package source moves, so no package `test` or `typecheck` is owed. No test file outside the script names it (`git grep`), so its self-test is its whole suite. CI owns `test:repo`, Test Core, the type-check lanes and `pnpm lint`; this PR's check-runs answer them.

**`skip-changeset`.** The file lives in the private root package (`"private": true`), and `scripts/` is in no published package's `files[]`. The label rides the create.

## Acceptance notes

- **The stamped date is the version run's day, as before.** On the `version-pr` lane that is the day of the last Version Packages refresh. It equals the npm publish day only when the PR merges the same UTC day as its last refresh, which held for 18.0.0. This PR does not change that; the header's `releaseDate` already states it.
- **Reported to the seat, not fixed here: a field written ahead of the CHANGELOG is rewritten BACK on a run that is not that GA's version run.** Measured on the same throwaway repository before `## 18.1.0` was added: a run on the pre-written `(current series: 18.1.0, released 2026-10-21)` produced `(current series: 18.0.0, released 2026-10-23)`. That is 18.0.0 with a date that is not 18.0.0's. This is the pre-existing stale-field path, which this PR keeps unchanged as the card requires. It is reachable from a version pass on a tree that carries such a field: a cut-rc.yml prerelease cut, or a manual run. `check-release-section-coverage` already reports such a field on `main` (advisory without `--strict`). Dedupe words: `sync-release-index-currency`, `ahead of the cut`, `rewritten back`, `current series`.
- The attribution block's first line is an HTML comment that the session requires, and `os-dev.md` forbids HTML comments in GitHub text. Same shape as PR #25354; reported as a deviation.
- The branch is the harness-pinned `claude/project-thread-1r2arf`. The claim (comment `6359770957`) records it as the identity.
